subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The Dodd-Frank Act
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Dodd-Frank Act usable.

hook.text: After the 2008 crash, Congress asked: how do we stop banks from destroying the economy again?

buildup.text: Dodd-Frank created stress tests, the Volcker Rule, and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

discovery.text: The Volcker Rule banned banks from making risky bets with depositor money for their own profit.

twist.text: Banks lobbied for years to weaken the law. Some provisions were rolled back by 2018.

climax.text: Financial reform is a tug of war. Regulators tighten, lobbyists loosen. The cycle never ends.

punchline.text: New rules after the crash. Lobbying started the next day.

quiz.question: What does the Volcker Rule prohibit?
options: Banks making risky bets with depositor money
